items.title: Physical braid implementation interface
items.statement_or_definition:
Let $V$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let
$\rho:B_n\to U(V)$ be a fixed mathematical braid representation. A **physical
implementation record** for a braid $b\in B_n$ consists of all of the following
data and hypotheses:

1. a finite-dimensional physical state space identified with $V$ on a specified
   low-energy sector;
2. a $C^2$ path $H(s)$ of Hermitian endomorphisms, $0\le s\le1$, and a
   norm-continuous constant-rank orthogonal spectral projection $P(s)$ that
   selects the followed band and is separated from its complement by a
   uniform positive full gap;
3. an explicit initial preparation isometry into $\operatorname{ran}P(0)$ and
   a stated slow-time schedule $T>0;$
4. a separate identification of the band's transported action for the chosen
   exchange path with $\rho(b)$, up to a stated scalar phase.

The first three clauses form an instance of the finite adiabatic path model
[[def-qa-36-finite-adiabatic-path-model]]. Under those hypotheses,
[[thm-qa-36-jrs-finite-adiabatic-bound]] bounds the deviation from ideal
adiabatic band following. That estimate does not establish that a material
realizes the fusion category, that the exchange path has the prescribed
holonomy, or that the initial state can be prepared at no cost. Locality,
temperature, quasiparticle separation, stray excitations, and tunnelling
require their own physical error model.

items.title: Special unitary groups are connected
items.statement_or_definition:
For every integer $n\ge1$, the matrix group
$$SU(n)=\{A\in M_n(\mathbb C):A^*A=I,\ \det A=1\}$$
is path connected.
proof_obligations:
1.1 The matrix $A$ is unitary and therefore normal. By [F1], choose a unitary
matrix $Q$ and real phases $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n$ such that
$A=Q\operatorname{diag}(e^{i\alpha_1},\ldots,e^{i\alpha_n})Q^*$.
Since $\det A=1$, [F2] gives $\sum_j\alpha_j=2\pi k$ for some integer $k$.
Replace $\alpha_1$ by $\alpha_1-2\pi k$; the eigenvalue is unchanged and the
sum of phases is now zero. This uses only finitely many eigenvalues.
[given, F1, F2, choose, algebra]

2.1 Define
$A(t)=Q\operatorname{diag}(e^{it\alpha_1},\ldots,e^{it\alpha_n})Q^*$ for
$0\le t\le1$. Each $A(t)$ is unitary by [F2], and
$\det A(t)=e^{it\sum_j\alpha_j}=1$, so $A(t)\in SU(n)$. The path is continuous by [F3], $A(0)=I$, and $A(1)=A$.
Thus every element is joined to the identity, proving path connectedness.
[given, F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Fixed-charge encoding and code projector
items.statement_or_definition:
Let $V=V(x^n\to c)\ne0$ be the finite-dimensional fixed-total-charge fusion
space for $n$ identical charges $x$, equipped with the unitary fusion-tree
inner product from [[def-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-basis]]. Let
$\mathcal C=\mathbb C^k$ with its ordered orthonormal computational basis,
where $k\ge1$. A **fixed-charge encoding** is an isometry
$J:\mathcal C\to V$, so $J^*J=I_{\mathcal C}$. Its code subspace is
$J\mathcal C$, and its code projector is
$$P:=JJ^*:V\to V.$$
An encoding records a chosen subspace of a fusion space; it does not identify
that subspace with an object of the fusion category.
proof_obligations:
1.1 By [F2], $P^*=(JJ^*)^*=(J^*)^*J^*=JJ^*=P$. Also
$P^2=JJ^*JJ^*=J(J^*J)J^*=JI_{\mathcal C}J^*=P$ by [F1]. Hence $P$ is an
orthogonal projection. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 For every $u\in\mathcal C$, $P(Ju)=JJ^*Ju=Ju$ by [F1], so
$J\mathcal C\subseteq\operatorname{ran}P$. Conversely $Pv=J(J^*v)$ lies
in $J\mathcal C$ for every $v\in V$, so
$\operatorname{ran}P\subseteq J\mathcal C$. Therefore
$\operatorname{ran}P=J\mathcal C$. [given, F1, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Logical block error and leakage amplitude
items.statement_or_definition:
Let $J:\mathcal C\to V$ be a fixed-charge encoding, $P=JJ^*$ its code
projector, $U\in U(\mathcal C)$ a logical target, and $W\in U(V)$ an ambient
unitary. Its zero-on-the-complement target extension is
$\widetilde U:=JUJ^*:V\to V$. Define the **logical block error** and
**leakage amplitude** by
$$\epsilon_{\mathrm{log}}(W,U):=\|PWP-\widetilde U\|_{\mathrm{op}},
\qquad
\epsilon_{\mathrm{leak}}(W):=\|(I-P)WP\|_{\mathrm{op}}.$$
Both are finite operator norms. The first measures the compressed block
against the target; the second measures transfer from the code into its
orthogonal complement. They diagnose different errors.
proof_obligations:
1.1 The maps $PWP-\widetilde U$ and $(I-P)WP$ are endomorphisms of $V$.
Because $V$ is finite dimensional, [F2] assigns a finite operator norm to
each map; the two quantities are therefore well defined. [given, F1, F2]

2.1 For a zero-leakage but logically incorrect boundary case, take
$V=\mathcal C=\mathbb C^2$, $J=P=I$, $W=I$, and
$U=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$. Then
$\epsilon_{\mathrm{leak}}=0$ and
$\epsilon_{\mathrm{log}}=\|I-U\|_{\mathrm{op}}=2$. This proves the two
quantities are not interchangeable. [given, F1, F2, algebra] ∎

items.title: Braid action on a fixed-charge fusion space
items.statement_or_definition:
Let $x$ be a simple charge in a unitary braided fusion category, let $n\ge2$,
and fix a total charge $c$ with nonzero multiplicity space
$V(x^n\to c)$. Use the left-associated fusion-tree basis. For the Artin
generator $\sigma_i$ that exchanges the $i$th and $(i+1)$st strands, let
$T_i$ be the specified sequence of $F$-moves that changes from the fixed tree
basis to a basis where those two charges fuse first, and let $R_i$ apply the
corresponding $R$-symbol on each pair-charge channel. Define
$$\rho_c(\sigma_i):=T_i^{-1}R_iT_i.$$
This defines the generator assignment. The next theorem proves that the
assignment descends from words to a well-defined group homomorphism. Word
products use matrix multiplication acting right-to-left on column vectors.
The abstract group in this definition is the Artin group
[[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]]; the positive crossing is the
generator convention used for the displayed $R$-symbols. If a motion is
described chronologically, its matrix product is written in reverse temporal
order.

items.title: Exact logical-block correctness forces zero leakage
items.statement_or_definition:
Let $J:\mathcal C\to V$ be an isometric encoding with $P=JJ^*$, let $U$ be
unitary on $\mathcal C$, and let $W$ be unitary on $V$. If the logical block
error $\|PWP-JUJ^*\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ is zero, then the leakage amplitude
$\|(I-P)WP\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ is zero.
proof_obligations:
1.1 Zero block error means $PWP=JUJ^*$ as operators on $V$. For every
$x\in\mathcal C$, $J^*J=I_{\mathcal C}$ gives
$PWJx=PWPJx=JUJ^*Jx=JUx$. By [F2], $\|WJx\|=\|x\|$ and
$\|PWJx\|=\|JUx\|=\|Ux\|=\|x\|$. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 The decomposition $WJx=PWJx+(I-P)WJx$ is orthogonal by [F1]. Its
Pythagorean identity and step 1.1 give
$\|(I-P)WJx\|^2=\|WJx\|^2-\|PWJx\|^2=0$ for every $x$. Hence
$(I-P)WJ=0$, and since $P=JJ^*$, $(I-P)WP=0$; its operator norm is zero.
[F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Block-target approximation bounds logical error and leakage
items.statement_or_definition:
Let $V=P V\oplus(I-P)V$ be an orthogonal decomposition of a finite-dimensional
Hilbert space, let $U$ and $W$ be unitary operators on the two summands, and
let $T:=U\oplus W$. If an ambient unitary $G$ satisfies
$\|G-T\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta$, then the logical block error of $G$ relative
to $U$ and its leakage amplitude both are at most $\delta$.
proof_obligations:
1.1 Since $T$ preserves both summands, $PTP=UP$ on $PV$ and
$(I-P)TP=0$. Thus $PGP-UP=P(G-T)P$. For any $y\in V$, the decomposition
$y=Py+(I-P)y$ is orthogonal, so the Pythagorean identity gives
$\|Py\|\le\|y\|$ and $\|(I-P)y\|\le\|y\|$. Applying the first inequality
to $y=(G-T)Px$ and to $x$, for every unit vector $x$, yields
$\|P(G-T)Px\|\le\|(G-T)Px\|\le\|G-T\|_{\mathrm{op}}$. Taking the maximum
in [F2] proves the norm is at most $\delta$. This is the logical block
error bound. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 Similarly $(I-P)GP=(I-P)(G-T)P$ because $(I-P)TP=0$. Use the second
contraction proved in step 1.1: for every unit $x$,
$\|(I-P)(G-T)Px\|\le\|(G-T)Px\|\le\|G-T\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta$.
Taking the maximum gives the leakage bound. [given, F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Ising–Majorana exchange interface
items.statement_or_definition:
Let $m\ge2$ and let $\mathcal H=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes m}$. A **Majorana
system of length $2m$** is a family of operators
$\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_{2m}\in\operatorname{End}(\mathcal H)$ satisfying
$$\gamma_j^*=\gamma_j,\qquad \gamma_j^2=I,\qquad
\gamma_j\gamma_k=-\gamma_k\gamma_j\quad(j\ne k).$$
Its parity operator is $\Pi=i^m\gamma_1\cdots\gamma_{2m}$. For each adjacent
pair, put
$$Q_1(j)=\frac{I-i\gamma_j\gamma_{j+1}}2,\qquad
Q_\psi(j)=\frac{I+i\gamma_j\gamma_{j+1}}2,\qquad
U_j=\exp\!\left(-\frac\pi4\gamma_j\gamma_{j+1}\right).$$

A **Majorana–Ising exchange interface** on a fixed parity sector consists of
such a system, a choice $\eta\in\{1,-1\}$ and the sector
$\mathcal H_\eta=\ker(\Pi-\eta I)$, together with the following explicit
model-identification hypotheses for every $1\le j<2m$: the Ising pair-charge
projections are identified with $Q_1(j),Q_\psi(j)$, and the exchange is
$R_1Q_1(j)+R_\psi Q_\psi(j)$ with the same relative phase
$R_\psi/R_1=i$. The last identity is required for all adjacent pairs as part
of the interface; the three-anyon supplier below establishes it only in its
stated sector and does not prove this all-$m$ identification.
proof_obligations:
1.1 Let $A_j=i\gamma_j\gamma_{j+1}$. The Majorana relations give
$A_j^*=A_j$ and $A_j^2=I$. Therefore
$Q_1(j)=(I-A_j)/2$ and $Q_\psi(j)=(I+A_j)/2$ are self-adjoint
idempotents, $Q_1(j)Q_\psi(j)=0$, and $Q_1(j)+Q_\psi(j)=I$. They are the
orthogonal complementary pair-channel projections stipulated by the
interface. [given, algebra]

1.2 Since $(\gamma_j\gamma_{j+1})^2=-I$, expansion of the exponential gives
$U_j=2^{-1/2}(I-\gamma_j\gamma_{j+1})$. Its restrictions to
$\operatorname{ran}Q_1(j)$ and $\operatorname{ran}Q_\psi(j)$ are respectively
$e^{-i\pi/4}I$ and $e^{i\pi/4}I$. Using the phase ratio in [F1] as imposed
for every generator by the interface, the channel exchange equals
$$R_1Q_1(j)+R_\psi Q_\psi(j)=R_1e^{i\pi/4}U_j.$$
Thus it differs from $U_j$ by one common scalar. [given, F1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Projective braid gate and operator metric
items.statement_or_definition:
Let $V\ne0$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let
$U(V)$ be its unitary group. Two unitaries are **projectively equivalent**
when $A=zB$ for some $z\in\mathbb C$ with $|z|=1$; write $[A]\in PU(V)$ for
the equivalence class. Define
$$d_P([A],[B]):=\min_{|z|=1}\|A-zB\|_{\mathrm{op}}.$$
This is the distance after quotienting by one common scalar phase. The phase
is minimized over the unit circle; it is not chosen independently in
different charge blocks.
proof_obligations:
1.1 The operator norm satisfies the triangle inequality: for every unit
vector $x$, $\|(S+T)x\|\le\|Sx\|+\|Tx\|\le\|S\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\|T\|_{\mathrm{op}}$,
so taking the maximum gives $\|S+T\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\|S\|_{\mathrm{op}}+
\|T\|_{\mathrm{op}}$. Scalar homogeneity follows from [F2] and the same
maximum definition. Thus
$|\|S\|_{\mathrm{op}}-\|T\|_{\mathrm{op}}|\le\|S-T\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ by applying
the triangle inequality twice. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 The formula is independent of representatives. If $A'=uA$ and $B'=vB$
with $|u|=|v|=1$, then
$\inf_{|z|=1}\|A'-zB'\|=\inf_{|z|=1}\|A-(u^{-1}zv)B\|$; as $z$ runs over the
unit circle, so does $u^{-1}zv$. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 The map $z\mapsto\|A-zB\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ is continuous: step 1.1 bounds
$|\|A-zB\|-\|A-wB\||\le\|(z-w)B\|=|z-w|\|B\|$. By [F3] and [F4] it attains
its minimum on the unit circle, so the infimum in the definition is a
minimum. Nonnegativity and symmetry follow from the norm axioms and the
substitution $z\mapsto\bar z$. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 For classes $[A],[B],[C]$, choose minimizing phases $z,w$ for the pairs
$(A,B)$ and $(B,C)$ by [F3]–[F4]. The triangle inequality gives
$\|A-zwC\|\le\|A-zB\|+\|zB-zwC\|=d_P([A],[B])+d_P([B],[C])$, so taking the
minimum over phases for $(A,C)$ proves the triangle inequality. If
$d_P([A],[B])=0$, a minimizing phase satisfies $A=zB$, so $[A]=[B]$.
Conversely equal classes have distance zero. Therefore $d_P$ is a metric on
$PU(V)$. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Six-anyon triple-encoded subspace and leakage complement
items.statement_or_definition:
Assume the Fibonacci fusion rules
$1\otimes x=x\otimes1=x$ and $\tau\otimes\tau=1\oplus\tau$, with each
listed summand of multiplicity one. For six ordered $\tau$ charges, let
$W_a$ be the fixed-input, fixed-total fusion space of total charge
$a\in\{1,\tau\}$ in the tree that first fuses leaves $1,2,3$ and $4,5,6$
separately, then fuses those triple outputs. Let
$V_a$ be the same fixed-charge space in the left-associated tree.

To identify these spaces, write
$A=((\tau_1\otimes\tau_2)\otimes\tau_3)$. Use the object associator
composite
$$g=(\alpha^{-1}_{A\otimes\tau_4,\tau_5,\tau_6})
\circ\alpha^{-1}_{A,\tau_4,\tau_5\otimes\tau_6}
\circ(\operatorname{id}_A\otimes\alpha_{\tau_4,\tau_5,\tau_6})$$
from the triple-grouped input tree to the left-associated tree. On a fusion
morphism $f$ into $a$, define $G_a(f)=f\circ g^{-1}:V_a$; this is a unitary
change of fusion-tree coordinates.

For one triple of total charge $\tau$, its two orthonormal path vectors are
indexed by the charge $x\in\{1,\tau\}$ after the first two anyons: both
$x\otimes\tau\to\tau$ channels have multiplicity one. Write these vectors as
$|x\rangle$. For $x,y\in\{1,\tau\}$ and $a\in\{1,\tau\}$, let $|x,y;a\rangle$
be the grouped-tree vector with first triple path $x$, first triple total
$\tau$, second triple path $y$, second triple total $\tau$, and final vertex
channel $\tau\otimes\tau\to a$. The last channel has multiplicity one. Define
$$\mathcal C_a:=G_a\bigl(\operatorname{span}\{|x,y;a\rangle:
x,y\in\{1,\tau\}\}\bigr)\subseteq V_a.$$
In the ordered basis
$(G_a|1,1;a\rangle,G_a|1,\tau;a\rangle,
G_a|\tau,1;a\rangle,G_a|\tau,\tau;a\rangle)$, the inclusion
$J_a:\mathbb C^4\to V_a$ is an isometry; its code projector is $P_a=J_aJ_a^*$.
The same ordered local triple paths are used for $a=1$ and $a=\tau$; only
the final pair-charge coordinate differs. The orthogonal complements are
called leakage spaces.
proof_obligations:
1.1 The fusion rule gives
$\dim V(\tau^2\to1)=\dim V(\tau^2\to\tau)=1$ and therefore
$\dim V(\tau^3\to1)=1$, $\dim V(\tau^3\to\tau)=2$. Applying the
fusion-tree count [F2] to the grouped tree, total charge $1$ receives one
basis vector from the $(1,1)$ triple-output pair and four from $(\tau,\tau)$,
so $\dim W_1=1+2\cdot2=5$. Total charge $\tau$ receives two vectors from
$(1,\tau)$, two from $(\tau,1)$, and four from $(\tau,\tau)$, so
$\dim W_\tau=2+2+4=8$. The map $G_a$ in [F4] is unitary, hence
$\dim V_1=5$ and $\dim V_\tau=8$. [A1, F2, F4, algebra]

1.2 Each selected triple-total-$\tau$ factor has its two paths $|1\rangle$
and $|\tau\rangle$, and the final $\tau\otimes\tau\to a$ vertex has
multiplicity one. Thus the four grouped-tree vectors $|x,y;a\rangle$ are admissible tree vectors by [F1] and form an
orthonormal family by [F2]. Applying the unitary $G_a$ preserves
orthonormality, so they define an isometric inclusion $J_a$; [F3] gives
the projector $P_a=J_aJ_a^*$ and $\dim\mathcal C_a=4$.
[F1, F2, F3, F4, given, algebra]

2.1 The orthogonal decompositions $V_a=\mathcal C_a\oplus\mathcal C_a^\perp$
then give $\dim\mathcal C_1^\perp=5-4=1$ and
$\dim\mathcal C_\tau^\perp=8-4=4$ by step 1.1. These code copies share the
same ordered local triple paths, while their final output charge differs.
This supplies the dimensions and path identification used in the two B6
blocks. [step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

items.title: Three-Fibonacci-anyon qubit matrices
items.statement_or_definition:
For three $\tau$ anyons of total charge $\tau$, the fusion space is
two-dimensional. Fix the chiral convention
$$F=\begin{pmatrix}\phi^{-1}&\phi^{-1/2}\\
\phi^{-1/2}&-\phi^{-1}\end{pmatrix},\qquad
r=R_\tau/R_1=e^{-3\pi i/5}.$$
After removing the common scalar $R_1$, the adjacent generators are
$$B_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,r),\qquad B_2=FB_1F.$$

The verification checks these matrices directly as a unitary $B_3$
representation. It uses the listed sector data as input and does not infer
global category coherence from this calculation.
proof_obligations:
1.1 Put $u=\phi^{-1}$ and $v=\phi^{-1/2}$. Since
$\phi^2=\phi+1$,
$u^2+u=1$ and $v^2=u$. Matrix multiplication then gives
$F^2=\begin{pmatrix}u^2+v^2&uv-uv\\uv-uv&u^2+v^2\end{pmatrix}=I$.
Both diagonal entries of $B_1$ have modulus one, so $B_1$ is unitary; $F$
is unitary because it is real and $F^*F=F^2=I$. The data in [F1] give
$r=R_\tau/R_1=e^{-3\pi i/5}$. Also $r^5=-1$ and
$r\ne-1$, so division of $r^5+1=0$ by $r+1$ gives
$r^4-r^3+r^2-r+1=0$. With $y=r+r^{-1}$, division by $r^2$ gives
$y^2-y-1=0$; since $y=2\cos(3\pi/5)<0$, it follows that $y=-u$ and
$r^2+ur+1=0$. Hence $B_2=FB_1F$ is unitary. [given, F1, algebra]

1.2 Write $B_2=\begin{pmatrix}p&q\\q&t\end{pmatrix}$, where
$p=u^2+ur$, $q=uv(1-r)$, and $t=u+u^2r$. Then
$$B_1B_2B_1=
\begin{pmatrix}p&qr\\qr&r^2t\end{pmatrix},\qquad
B_2B_1B_2=
\begin{pmatrix}p^2+q^2r&q(p+rt)\\q(p+rt)&q^2+t^2r\end{pmatrix}.$$
The relations $r^2=-ur-1$ and $u^3=2u-1$ give $p+rt=r$; expanding the
remaining diagonal entries and using $u^2+u=1$, $v^2=u$, and
$r^2+ur+1=0$ gives $p^2+q^2r=p$ and $q^2+t^2r=-p$. Thus both matrices reduce to
$$\begin{pmatrix}u^2+ur&uvr(1-r)\\uvr(1-r)&-(u^2+ur)\end{pmatrix}.$$
The Artin relation follows entry by entry. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 The off-diagonal entry of $B_1B_2-B_2B_1$ is
$q(1-r)=uv(1-r)^2\ne0$, because $u,v\ne0$ and $r\ne1$. Thus the generators
do not commute. They are not two copies of a single diagonal phase gate in
the same fusion basis. [given, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

items.title: Three-Ising-anyon braid matrices are Clifford
items.statement_or_definition:
In the three-$\sigma$, total-$\sigma$ Ising sector, use
$F=H=2^{-1/2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}$,
$R_1=e^{-i\pi/8}$, and $R_\psi=e^{3i\pi/8}$. After removing the common phase
$R_1$, the two projective braid generators are
$$B_1=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&i\end{pmatrix},\qquad
B_2=H B_1 H.$$
proof_obligations:
1.1 By [F3], $R_\psi/R_1=i$. Removing $R_1$ gives
$B_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,i)$, and recoupling by $H=H^{-1}$ gives
$B_2=HB_1H$. Both are unitary because $H$ and $B_1$ are unitary. Put
$a=(1+i)/2$ and $b=(1-i)/2$, so $B_2=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\b&a\end{pmatrix}$.
Direct multiplication, using $a^2+ib^2=a$, $ab(1+i)=ib$, and
$b^2+ia^2=-a$, gives
$$B_1B_2B_1=\begin{pmatrix}a&ib\\ib&-a\end{pmatrix}
=B_2B_1B_2.$$
Thus these matrices define a unitary representation of the two-generator
Artin presentation of $B_3$, independently of any all-label Ising
coherence claim. [F3, algebra]

1.2 Direct multiplication gives
$B_1XB_1^*=Y$, $B_1YB_1^*=-X$, and $B_1ZB_1^*=Z$; also
$B_2XB_2^*=X$, $B_2YB_2^*=Z$, and $B_2ZB_2^*=-Y$. Thus each generator
conjugates every Pauli matrix to a signed Pauli matrix. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

2.1 Products and inverses of Pauli normalizers again normalize the Pauli
group: for normalizers $A,B$, $(AB)\mathcal P(AB)^*
=A(B\mathcal P B^*)A^*=\mathcal P$, and the inverse property follows by
conjugating the equality $A\mathcal P A^*=\mathcal P$ by $A^*$. The scalar
phase removed in step 1.1 has trivial conjugation action, so the physical
braids are projectively Clifford in this sector. [F2, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

items.title: The braid phase is a common determinant character
items.statement_or_definition:
Fix the Fibonacci convention with common exchange scalar $R_1$. Let
$e:B_n\to\mathbb Z$ be exponent sum, sending each Artin generator $\sigma_i$
to $1$. If $\widetilde\rho$ is the generator-normalized representation
$\widetilde\rho(\sigma_i)=R_1^{-1}\rho(\sigma_i)$, then for every braid $b$
and every total-charge block,
$$\rho(b)=R_1^{e(b)}\widetilde\rho(b).$$
The scalar is the same on every total-charge block and every spectator
multiplicity. It is a global phase for an uncontrolled fixed-sector
computation; under coherent control it is a relative phase and must be
tracked.
proof_obligations:
1.1 Exponent sum is well defined on the Artin group: both sides of every
adjacent braid relation have sum $3$, both sides of every distant commutation
relation have sum $2$, and inverse cancellation changes the sum by $0$.
Thus $e:B_n\to\mathbb Z$ is a homomorphism. [given, algebra]

1.2 For a word $b=\sigma_{i_1}^{\epsilon_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_k}^{\epsilon_k}$,
each positive generator contributes $R_1$ and each inverse contributes
$R_1^{-1}$ to the scalar, by [A1]. The scalar product is therefore
$R_1^{\epsilon_1+\cdots+\epsilon_k}=R_1^{e(b)}$, while the remaining
normalized matrices multiply to $\widetilde\rho(b)$. Since every relation
preserves exponent sum, this factorization is independent of the word
representative. [A1, step 1.1, algebra]

2.1 The same scalar multiplies every charge block, so [F2] applies to an
uncontrolled isolated sector. Under coherent control the scalar multiplies
only the active branch, and [F3] shows it becomes a relative phase; it cannot
be discarded without recording or correcting it. [F2, F3, step 1.2] ∎

items.title: Fibonacci B6 path projectors satisfy the braid relations
items.statement_or_definition:
Use the Fibonacci fusion rule $\tau\otimes\tau=1\oplus\tau$ and the
fixed-chirality data
$F^{\tau\tau\tau}_\tau=\begin{pmatrix}\phi^{-1}&\phi^{-1/2}\\
\phi^{-1/2}&-\phi^{-1}\end{pmatrix}$ and
$r=R_\tau/R_1=e^{-3\pi i/5}$. The fixed-total-charge B6 path bases are

$$\mathcal P_1=\{0101010,0101110,0110110,0111010,0111110\},$$

$$\mathcal P_\tau=\{0101011,0101101,0101111,0110101,0110111,0111011,0111101,0111111\},$$

where each path is $(x_0,\ldots,x_6)$, $x_0=0$ is the unit label,
$x_1=1$ is $\tau$, and adjacent labels obey the fusion rule. For
$d_0=1,d_1=\phi$, define $E_i$ on either path basis by
$$(E_i)_{x,y}=
\begin{cases}
\sqrt{d_{x_i}d_{y_i}}/d_{x_{i-1}},
&x_j=y_j\ (j\ne i),\ x_{i-1}=x_{i+1}=y_{i-1}=y_{i+1},\\
0,&\text{otherwise,}
\end{cases}
\qquad P_i:=\phi^{-1}E_i.$$
Then $P_i$ are orthogonal projections, have ranks $2$ on $\mathcal P_1$
and $3$ on $\mathcal P_\tau$, satisfy
$P_iP_{i+1}P_i=\phi^{-2}P_i$ and commute at separation at least two.
Consequently $B_i=rI+(1-r)P_i$ are unitary matrices satisfying the Artin
relations of $B_6$, with
$\det B_i=r^3$ on $V(\tau^6\to1)$ and $\det B_i=r^5$ on
$V(\tau^6\to\tau)$.
proof_obligations:
1.1 Starting with $(x_0,x_1)=(0,1)$, the fusion rule permits only $x_{j+1}=1$
when $x_j=0$, and permits $x_{j+1}\in\{0,1\}$ when $x_j=1$. Enumerating the
five remaining transitions with endpoint $x_6=0$ or $1$ gives exactly the
two path sets displayed in the Statement; hence the block dimensions are
$5$ and $8$. Also $r^5=-1$ and $r\ne-1$, so
$r^4-r^3+r^2-r+1=0$. For $y=r+r^{-1}$, division by $r^2$ gives
$y^2-y-1=0$; since $y=2\cos(3\pi/5)<0$, $y=-\phi^{-1}$. Thus
$r^2+\phi^{-1}r+1=0$. [given, A1, F2, construct, algebra]

1.2 In a fixed left-tree basis, $P_i$ is the projection onto pair channel
$1$. The $F$-move gives the only nontrivial local block, on the two
intermediate channels $(1,\tau)$:
$$\begin{pmatrix}\phi^{-2}&\phi^{-3/2}\\
\phi^{-3/2}&\phi^{-1}\end{pmatrix}.$$
Its square equals itself because
$\phi^{-4}+\phi^{-3}=\phi^{-2}$,
$\phi^{-3/2}(\phi^{-2}+\phi^{-1})=\phi^{-3/2}$, and
$\phi^{-3}+\phi^{-2}=\phi^{-1}$; its entries are real symmetric. When the
surrounding charge is the unit, the only allowed pair-channel block is
$[1]$. Thus each $P_i=P_i^*=P_i^2$.
Counting the diagonal entries of these blocks on the listed paths gives
$\operatorname{tr}P_i=2$ on $\mathcal P_1$ and $3$ on $\mathcal P_\tau$,
so these are the ranks. [given, A1, F2, algebra]

2.1 On the nontrivial three-strand total-$\tau$ block, the adjacent
projections are $P=|e_1\rangle\langle e_1|$ and
$Q=|f_1\rangle\langle f_1|$, where
$f_1=(\phi^{-1},\phi^{-1/2})$ is the first column of $F$. Therefore
$PQP=|\langle e_1,f_1\rangle|^2P=\phi^{-2}P$ and symmetrically
$QPQ=\phi^{-2}Q$. In the one-dimensional total-$1$ block both adjacent
projections are zero, so the same identities hold. Tensoring with spectator
path factors leaves these identities unchanged. Operators on disjoint pairs
commute by the interchange law for tensor products. [A1, algebra]

2.2 Put $q_0=\phi^{-2}$. For adjacent $P=P_i,Q=P_{i+1}$ and
$s=1-r$, direct expansion using $P^2=P$, $Q^2=Q$,
$PQP=q_0P$, and $QPQ=q_0Q$ gives
$$[rI+sP][rI+sQ][rI+sP]-[rI+sQ][rI+sP][rI+sQ]
=s\bigl(r+q_0s^2\bigr)(P-Q).$$
Because $r+r^{-1}=-\phi^{-1}$,
$\bigl(r+q_0(1-r)^2\bigr)/r
=1+\phi^{-2}(r+r^{-1}-2)
=1-\phi^{-2}(\phi^{-1}+2)=0$; here $\phi^{-1}+2=\phi^2$.
Thus the adjacent braid relation holds. [A1, step 2.1, algebra]

3.1 Since $P_i$ is an orthogonal projection and $|r|=1$, $B_i$ acts by
$1$ on $\operatorname{ran}P_i$ and by $r$ on its orthogonal complement, so
it is unitary. The distant commutation and adjacent relation from steps
2.1–2.2 are the defining Artin relations, hence the matrices represent $B_6$.
The rank table gives rank $2$ on the five-dimensional block and rank $3$ on
the eight-dimensional block, so $\det B_i=r^{5-2}=r^3$ and
$\det B_i=r^{8-3}=r^5$, respectively. [given, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 2.2, algebra] ∎

items.title: Fibonacci coefficient ring and its exact mod-31 specialization
items.statement_or_definition:
Let $r=e^{-3\pi i/5}$, $\phi=(1+\sqrt5)/2=1-r-r^{-1}$, and
$s=\sqrt\phi>0$. Then
$$\mathbb Z[r,s]\cong
\mathbb Z[x,y]\big/\bigl(x^4-x^3+x^2-x+1,\ y^2-(1-x-x^{-1})\bigr),$$
where $x^{-1}=x^9$. The assignment
$$r\mapsto15,\qquad r^{-1}\mapsto29,\qquad
\phi\mapsto19,\qquad s\mapsto9$$
defines a ring homomorphism to $\mathbb F_{31}$. The elements $r$ and
$\phi$ map to nonzero units, and conjugation of coefficients is handled by
$r\mapsto r^{-1}$ before reduction.
proof_obligations:
1.1 The number $r$ is a primitive tenth root of unity, so its minimal
polynomial is $\Phi_{10}(x)=x^4-x^3+x^2-x+1$ and $[\mathbb Q(r):\mathbb Q]=4$.
Its maximal real subfield is $\mathbb Q(\sqrt5)$, and the nontrivial
conjugate of $\phi$ is $(1-\sqrt5)/2=-\phi^{-1}$; hence the field norm of
$\phi$ from $\mathbb Q(\sqrt5)$ to $\mathbb Q$ is $-1$. Therefore $\phi$ is
not a square in that real subfield, since the norm of a square would be a
nonnegative rational square. [given, A1, algebra]

1.2 If $u\in\mathbb Q(r)$ satisfied $u^2=\phi$, complex conjugation would
give $\bar u^2=\phi$, hence $\bar u=u$ or $\bar u=-u$. In the first case
$u\in\mathbb Q(\sqrt5)$, contradicting step 1.1. In the second case $u$ is
purely imaginary in the chosen embedding, so $u^2$ is nonpositive real,
contrary to $\phi>0$. Thus $Y^2-\phi$ is irreducible over $\mathbb Q(r)$
and $[\mathbb Q(r,s):\mathbb Q]=8$. The displayed monic relations therefore
give the full degree-eight presentation; no additional relation is being
assumed. [given, step 1.1, algebra]

2.1 In $\mathbb F_{31}$, $15^{-1}=29$,
$\Phi_{10}(15)=0$, $1-15-29=19$, and $9^2=19$. Thus the assignments satisfy
both defining relations and extend to the stated ring homomorphism. The
images $15$ and $19$ are nonzero, so $r,\phi$ and their powers are units;
all denominators in the path projectors and normalized braid matrices are
therefore invertible after specialization. [given, A1, step 1.2, algebra]

2.2 In the number field, complex conjugation fixes $\phi,s$ and sends
$r$ to $r^{-1}$. Therefore a coefficient involving conjugation is first
rewritten with $r^{-1}$ and only then reduced by $r^{-1}\mapsto29$.
No conjugation operation on $\mathbb F_{31}$ is required. [given, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Logical error and leakage add under code-preserving gate approximation
items.statement_or_definition:
Let $P$ be a code projection on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space $V$. Let
$W_1,\ldots,W_G$ be ideal unitaries preserving $\operatorname{ran}P$, and let
$V_1,\ldots,V_G$ be physical unitaries with
$\|V_j-W_j\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta_j$. If
$V_{\mathrm{tot}}=V_G\cdots V_1$ and $W_{\mathrm{tot}}=W_G\cdots W_1$,
then, with empty products equal to $I$ and empty sums equal to $0$,
$$\|V_{\mathrm{tot}}-W_{\mathrm{tot}}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le\sum_{j=1}^{G}\delta_j.$$
Consequently the logical block error and leakage amplitude relative to the
code action of $W_{\mathrm{tot}}$ are each at most $\sum_j\delta_j$.
proof_obligations:
1.1 If $G=0$, both products are the empty product $I$ and the sum of errors
is $0$, so the full-space error is $0$; [F2] then gives zero logical block
error and zero leakage. [given, F2, algebra]

1.2 For $G\ge1$, insert and subtract the mixed products to obtain the exact telescoping
identity
$$V_G\cdots V_1-W_G\cdots W_1
=\sum_{j=1}^{G}V_G\cdots V_{j+1}(V_j-W_j)W_{j-1}\cdots W_1.$$
It follows by expanding the sum: consecutive terms cancel, leaving only
$V_G\cdots V_1-W_G\cdots W_1$. Every outer product is unitary, so its
operator norm is one and each summand has norm at most $\delta_j$. The
triangle inequality proves the displayed sum bound. [given, algebra]

2.1 The product $W_{\mathrm{tot}}$ preserves the code because each factor
does. Apply [F2] with
$\delta=\|V_{\mathrm{tot}}-W_{\mathrm{tot}}\|_{\mathrm{op}}$; step 1.1
bounds this by $\sum_j\delta_j$ using step 1.2 when $G\ge1$ and step 1.1
when $G=0$. This gives the claimed logical error and leakage bounds, including
on arbitrary ambient states before projection. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

items.title: Unitary Artin braid representation on fixed-charge fusion spaces
items.statement_or_definition:
For a unitary braided fusion category, a simple charge $x$, and a fixed total
charge $c$, the operators in
[[def-qc-tqc-braid-action-from-fusion-data]] define a unitary group
homomorphism
$$\rho_c:B_n\longrightarrow U(V(x^n\to c)).$$
In particular, the adjacent Artin relations and distant commutation relations
hold in each fixed-charge block.
proof_obligations:
1.1 By [F2], each generator matrix is a product of unitary operators: $T_i$
and $T_i^{-1}$ are unitary changes of orthonormal fusion-tree basis, and
$R_i$ is unitary on every orthogonal pair-charge summand. Therefore
$\rho_c(\sigma_i)^*\rho_c(\sigma_i)=I$ and every generator, as well as its
inverse, is unitary. [given, F2, algebra]

2.1 By [F1], the local categorical braidings on the full tensor power satisfy
the Artin relations and define a homomorphism for the fixed parenthesization.
Finite semisimplicity and orthogonality in [F2] decompose that tensor power
into total-charge blocks; naturality of the braiding makes each block
invariant, so restriction to $V(x^n\to c)$ preserves the same relations.
In the fusion-tree basis, these restricted operators are exactly
$T_i^{-1}R_iT_i$ by the definition in
[[def-qc-tqc-braid-action-from-fusion-data]]. The pentagon and hexagon
coordinate identities in [F2] identify those matrices with the same
parenthesized composites; distant generators commute because they act on
disjoint tensor factors. Hence the restricted assignment is a unitary
representation of the Artin presentation. [F1, F2, given, algebra] ∎

items.title: A controlled braid phase is observable
items.statement_or_definition:
A scalar phase that is irrelevant for an uncontrolled fixed-sector braid
remains irrelevant when that braid is coherently controlled.
proof_obligations:
1.1 Uncontrolled on $\mathbb C$, the gates $I$ and $-I$ differ by the scalar
$-1$, so they have the same projective class by [F1]. [given, F1, algebra]

1.2 The controlled $I$ is the identity, so it leaves the control in $|+\rangle$
and the $+$ outcome has probability $1$. The controlled $-I$ is
$\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$ on the control; it maps $|+\rangle$ to $|-\rangle$,
so the same outcome has probability $0$. Thus the controlled outcome laws
differ, refuting the statement. [given, F2, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Exact, projective, and encoded braid universality
items.statement_or_definition:
Let $\Gamma\le U(V)$ be a subgroup acting on a nonzero finite-dimensional
Hilbert space $V$. It is **exactly universal** on $V$ when $\Gamma=U(V)$,
**projectively exactly universal** when its image in $PU(V)$ is all of
$PU(V)$, and **projectively dense** when that image is dense in the metric
$d_P$ of [[def-qc-tqc-projective-gate-and-metric]].

For an encoding $J:\mathcal C\to V$ with code projector $P=JJ^*$, the action
is **approximate logical-and-leakage universal** if for every
$U\in U(\mathcal C)$ and every $\epsilon>0$ there is $W\in\Gamma$ and a
phase $z\in U(1)$ such that
$$\|PWP-zJUJ^*\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\epsilon,\qquad
\|(I-P)WP\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\epsilon.$$
This last notion includes a leakage bound as a separate requirement; projective
density on one fusion block alone does not supply it.

items.title: The projective one-qubit group is SO(3)
items.statement_or_definition:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Give $PU(2)$ the quotient metric from
[[def-qc-tqc-projective-gate-and-metric]]. The map
$$q:SU(2)\longrightarrow PU(2),\qquad q(A)=[A],$$
is a two-sheeted covering with kernel $\{I,-I\}$. It induces a topological
group isomorphism $SU(2)/\{\pm I\}\cong PU(2)\cong SO(3)$.
proof_obligations:
1.1 The determinant of a unitary $A\in U(2)$ has modulus one, since
$1=\det(A^*A)=\overline{\det A}\det A$. Write $\det A=e^{i\theta}$ by [F4]
and put $\lambda=e^{-i\theta/2}$. Then $|\lambda|=1$ and
$\det(\lambda A)=\lambda^2\det A=1$, so $\lambda A\in SU(2)$ and
$q(\lambda A)=q(A)$. Thus $q$ is onto. [given, F4, algebra]

1.2 If $A\in SU(2)$ and $q(A)=[I]$, then $A=\lambda I$ for some $|\lambda|=1$.
The determinant condition gives $\lambda^2=1$, hence $\lambda=\pm1$.
Conversely $I$ and $-I$ have the same projective class. Therefore
$\ker q=\{\pm I\}$, and two matrices have the same $q$-image exactly when
they differ by this kernel. [given, step 1.1, algebra]

2.1 The map $q$ is continuous: by [F1],
$d_P(q(A),q(B))\le\|A-B\|_{\mathrm{op}}$. Identify $M_2(\mathbb C)$ with
$\mathbb R^8$. The equations $A^*A=I$ and $\det A=1$ define a closed subset,
and each matrix entry is bounded in modulus by $1$ because each column has
norm $1$. Thus $SU(2)$ is compact by [F2]. The metric space $PU(2)$ is
Hausdorff by [F1]. If $F\subseteq SU(2)$ is closed, then it is compact and
$q(F)$ is compact, hence closed by [F3]. It is a quotient map: if $q^{-1}(W)$ is open, then
$q^{-1}(PU(2)\setminus W)$ is closed; surjectivity and closedness of $q$
make its image $PU(2)\setminus W$ closed, so $W$ is open. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 By [F5] and step 1.2, $q$ and $\rho$ have exactly the same fibers.
There is therefore a unique bijective group homomorphism
$\bar\rho:PU(2)\to SO(3)$ with $\bar\rho(q(A))=\rho(A)$. It is continuous
because $q$ is a quotient map and $\rho=\bar\rho\circ q$ is continuous.
The space $PU(2)=q(SU(2))$ is compact, while $SO(3)$ is Hausdorff as a
subspace of the real $3\times3$ matrix space. A continuous bijection from
a compact space to a Hausdorff space is a homeomorphism: images of closed
sets are compact and therefore closed by [F3]. Hence $\bar\rho$ is a
topological group isomorphism. Since $q$ is a quotient map and its fibers
are exactly the cosets of $\{\pm I\}$ by step 1.2, the induced map
$SU(2)/\{\pm I\}\to PU(2)$ is also a homeomorphism. The covering sheets
for $q$ are carried from those of $\rho$ by this homeomorphism, so $q$ is a
two-sheeted covering.
[A1, F3, F5, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Exact five-dimensional Fibonacci B6 density
items.statement_or_definition:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. In the normalized Fibonacci B6 representation on
$V(\tau^6\to1)\cong\mathbb C^5$, the closure of the braid image in $U(5)$
contains $SU(5)$.
proof_obligations:
1.1 Write $u=\phi^{-1}$ and $r=R_\tau/R_1=e^{-3\pi i/5}$ by [F8]. The
fusion-tree recurrence [F7] gives
$\dim V(\tau^2\to1)=\dim V(\tau^2\to\tau)=1$,
$\dim V(\tau^3\to1)=1$, $\dim V(\tau^3\to\tau)=2$,
and $\dim V(\tau^4\to1)=2$. The five paths in $\mathcal P_1$ therefore
decompose by the charge of the first three strands as one dimension from
charge $1$, and $2\cdot2=4$ dimensions from charge $\tau$: the latter are
two copies of the same two-dimensional three-strand block. On the first summand $C:=B_1B_2^{-1}$ is $1$. On
each two-dimensional summand, $B_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,r)$ and
$B_2=FB_1F$ with $F^2=I$, so direct multiplication gives
$\det C=1$ and
$\operatorname{tr}C=r+r^{-1}+(2-r-r^{-1})u^2=u^2=\phi^{-2}$; the last
equality uses $u^2+u=1$, since $(2+u)u^2=1$. Consequently the full spectrum
is $1,e^{i\theta},e^{-i\theta}$, with the last two eigenvalues each repeated
twice and $2\cos\theta=\phi^{-2}$. [F1, F7, F8, A2, algebra]

1.2 The algebraic number $\phi^{-2}$ has minimal polynomial
$x^2-3x+1$, whose other root is $\phi^2>2$. If $e^{i\theta}$ were a root of
unity, then $e^{i\theta}+e^{-i\theta}$ and every algebraic conjugate of that
sum would be sums of two roots of unity and therefore have absolute value at
most $2$. The conjugate $\phi^2>2$ contradicts this. Thus
$\theta/(2\pi)$ is irrational. [given, step 1.1, algebra]

2.1 Let $H$ be the closure of the normalized B6 image in $U(5)$. The powers
of $C$ contain a dense subgroup of the circle
$\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{it}I_2,e^{-it}I_2)$, by [F3] and step 1.2.
Therefore the nonzero tangent $X=C-C^{-1}$ belongs to
$\operatorname{Lie}(H)$. [F3, step 1.2, construct]

3.1 Define $Y_0=X$ and, with $\operatorname{Ad}_i(Y)=B_iYB_i^{-1}$,
define the remaining $23$ words in order by
$$
Y_1=\operatorname{Ad}_1Y_0,\ Y_2=\operatorname{Ad}_2Y_0,\ Y_3=\operatorname{Ad}_3Y_0,\ 
Y_4=[Y_3,Y_0],\ Y_5=[Y_3,Y_1],\ Y_6=[Y_3,Y_2],\
Y_7=\operatorname{Ad}_3Y_1,\ Y_8=\operatorname{Ad}_3Y_2,\
Y_9=\operatorname{Ad}_2Y_3,\ Y_{10}=\operatorname{Ad}_4Y_3,
$$
$$
Y_{11}=\operatorname{Ad}_2Y_4,\ Y_{12}=\operatorname{Ad}_4Y_4,\
Y_{13}=\operatorname{Ad}_4Y_5,\ Y_{14}=\operatorname{Ad}_4Y_6,\
Y_{15}=[Y_{10},Y_3],\ Y_{16}=[Y_{10},Y_4],\
Y_{17}=[Y_{10},Y_5],\ Y_{18}=[Y_{10},Y_6],\
Y_{19}=[Y_{10},Y_7],\ Y_{20}=[Y_{10},Y_8],\
Y_{21}=[Y_{10},Y_9],\
Y_{22}=[Y_{12},Y_0],\ Y_{23}=[Y_{12},Y_1].
$$
Conjugation by an element of $H$ preserves $\operatorname{Lie}(H)$, and
[F4] makes that Lie algebra bracket closed, so every $Y_j$ lies in it.
Each is traceless and skew-Hermitian: this holds for $X$ because $C$ is
unitary with spectrum invariant under inversion, and is preserved by unitary
conjugation and commutators. [F1, F4, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 By [F2], every coefficient of the $Y_j$ matrices lies in
$\mathbb Z[r,\sqrt\phi]$ with all denominators units. Reduce coefficients
modulo $31$ using $r\mapsto15$, $r^{-1}\mapsto29$, $\phi\mapsto19$,
$\sqrt\phi\mapsto9$; for conjugated coefficients first replace $r$ by
$r^{-1}$ in the number field. The exact integer-arithmetic certificate
`research/scaffold-audit-2026-10-16/topological-quantum-computing/b6-lie-rank-certificate.py`
forms the $24\times24$ matrix whose rows are the first $24$ row-major
coordinates of $Y_0,\ldots,Y_{23}$ and returns determinant $17$ in
$\mathbb F_{31}$. Since the reduction is a ring homomorphism, a zero
algebraic determinant would reduce to zero; the determinant is therefore
nonzero over $\mathbb C$. Tracelessness lets the omitted coordinate be
recovered from the other $24$, so the $Y_j$ are linearly independent.
[F2, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 The determinant of each $B_i$ is $r^3$ by [F1], so
$\det(H)\subseteq\langle r^3\rangle$ is finite. The connected group $H^0$
therefore has determinant $1$, and
$\operatorname{Lie}(H)=\operatorname{Lie}(H^0)\subseteq\mathfrak{su}(5)$.
Step 3.1 places $24$ linearly independent traceless skew-Hermitian matrices
in this Lie algebra; by [F5], its dimension is $24$, so
$\operatorname{Lie}(H)=\mathfrak{su}(5)$. Thus $H^0$ has full dimension and
is an open subgroup of $SU(5)$. By [F6], $SU(5)$ is connected; an open
subgroup is also closed because its complement is a union of open cosets.
Hence $H^0=SU(5)$, and the closure contains $SU(5)$. [A1, A2, F1, F4, F5, F6, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Exact eight-dimensional Fibonacci B6 density
items.statement_or_definition:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. In the normalized Fibonacci B6 representation on
$V(\tau^6\to\tau)\cong\mathbb C^8$, the closure of the braid image in $U(8)$
contains $SU(8)$.
proof_obligations:
1.1 The fusion rule and $F/R$ convention in [F8], together with recurrence
[F7], give
$\dim V(\tau^3\to1)=1$, $\dim V(\tau^3\to\tau)=2$, and
$\dim V(\tau^4\to\tau)=3$. The eight paths in $\mathcal P_\tau$ thus
decompose by the first-three-charge label: charge $1$ contributes
$1\cdot2=2$ dimensions, and charge $\tau$ contributes
$V(\tau^3\to\tau)\otimes V(\tau\otimes\tau^3\to\tau)$ of
dimension $2\cdot3=6$.
The operator $C:=B_1B_2^{-1}$ is identity on the first summand. On the
two-dimensional first-three charge-$\tau$ factor it has determinant $1$ and
trace $\phi^{-2}$, so the full spectrum of $C$ is $1$ with multiplicity $2$
and $e^{i\theta},e^{-i\theta}$ each with multiplicity $3$, where
$2\cos\theta=\phi^{-2}$. [F1, F7, F8, A2, algebra]

1.2 The minimal polynomial of $\phi^{-2}$ is $x^2-3x+1$, whose other root
is $\phi^2>2$. If $e^{i\theta}$ were a root of unity, every algebraic
conjugate of its trace $e^{i\theta}+e^{-i\theta}$ would be a sum of two roots
of unity and have absolute value at most $2$, contradicting the conjugate
$\phi^2$. Thus $\theta/(2\pi)$ is irrational. [given, step 1.1, algebra]

2.1 By [F3], powers of $C$ are dense in the circle
$T=\operatorname{diag}(I_2,e^{it}I_3,e^{-it}I_3)$ after choosing an
eigenbasis. Let $H$ be the closure of the normalized B6 image in $U(8)$.
Then $T\subseteq H$, so the nonzero tangent $X=C-C^{-1}$ lies in
$\operatorname{Lie}(H)$. [F3, step 1.2, construct]

3.1 Starting with $Z_0=X$, construct a list as follows, all over
$\mathbb F_{31}$ for the independence tests: repeatedly scan
$\operatorname{Ad}_i(Z_j)=B_iZ_jB_i^{-1}$ in current-list order $j$ and
generator order $i=1,\ldots,5$, appending a word exactly when its specialized
row is independent of previous rows. Using the resulting list as a snapshot,
scan commutators $[Z_j,Z_i]$ in lexicographic order $j>i$, again appending
exactly the independent rows. Repeat full rounds until none is appended.
Each accepted word is an adjoint or bracket applied to earlier Lie algebra
elements, so it lifts to $\operatorname{Lie}(H)$. Unitary conjugation and
commutators preserve traceless skew-Hermitian matrices. [F1, F4, step 2.1, construct]

4.1 [F2] makes reduction of every coefficient and denominator in these words
well defined. The exact integer-arithmetic certificate
`research/scaffold-audit-2026-10-16/topological-quantum-computing/b6-su8-lie-rank-certificate.py`
selects 63 words by the procedure of step 3.1 (the script labels them
$Y_0,\ldots,Y_{62}$; this proof renames them $Z_0,\ldots,Z_{62}$) and
returns determinant $22$ for the $63\times63$ minor formed from the first
$63$ row-major coordinates of these matrices. A zero algebraic determinant
would map to zero in $\mathbb F_{31}$; since $22\ne0$, the exact determinant
is nonzero. The omitted coordinate is the final diagonal entry, determined
by trace zero. Thus the selected traceless skew-Hermitian matrices are
linearly independent over $\mathbb C$. [F2, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 By [F5], $\mathfrak{su}(8)$ has real dimension $63$. Step 4.1 supplies
$63$ independent elements of $\operatorname{Lie}(H)$, so
$\operatorname{Lie}(H)=\mathfrak{su}(8)$. Each $B_i$ has determinant
$r^{8-3}=r^5$ by [F1], hence $\det(H)\subseteq\langle r^5\rangle$ is finite.
The identity component therefore lies in $SU(8)$ and has full dimension;
it is open there. By [F6], $SU(8)$ is connected, so the identity component
equals $SU(8)$. Hence the B6 closure contains $SU(8)$. [A1, A2, F1, F4, F5, F6, step 4.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Even-Majorana Ising exchanges normalize logical Paulis
items.statement_or_definition:
Assume a Majorana–Ising exchange interface as defined in
[[def-qc-tqc-ising-majorana-interface]]. Let
$\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_{2m}$ be Majorana operators on the
$2^m$-dimensional fermionic Fock space, with
$\gamma_j^*=\gamma_j$, $\gamma_j^2=I$, and
$\gamma_j\gamma_k=-\gamma_k\gamma_j$ for $j\ne k$. On either fixed
eigenspace of the total parity
$$\Pi=i^m\gamma_1\gamma_2\cdots\gamma_{2m},$$
the adjacent Ising exchanges, up to their common physical scalar, are
$$U_j=\exp(-\pi\gamma_j\gamma_{j+1}/4),\qquad 1\le j<2m.$$
For $m\ge2$ they normalize the logical Pauli group on the $m-1$ encoded
qubits. Their braid-only projective image is finite and is not dense in
$PU(2^{m-1})$.
proof_obligations:
1.1 Reordering the $2m$ Majorana factors gives
$(\gamma_1\cdots\gamma_{2m})^*=(-1)^m\gamma_1\cdots\gamma_{2m}$ and
$(\gamma_1\cdots\gamma_{2m})^2=(-1)^mI$. Therefore $\Pi^*=\Pi$ and
$\Pi^2=I$. Also $\Pi\gamma_j=-\gamma_j\Pi$ for each $j$, so $\gamma_1$
bijects the $+1$ and $-1$ eigenspaces; each has dimension $2^{m-1}$.
Since each product $\gamma_j\gamma_{j+1}$ commutes with $\Pi$, every
$U_j$, being a function of that product, preserves both parity sectors. [given, algebra]

1.2 Put $A_j=i\gamma_j\gamma_{j+1}$. Then $A_j^*=A_j$ and $A_j^2=I$, so
$Q_1=(I-A_j)/2$ and $Q_\psi=(I+A_j)/2$ are orthogonal complementary
projections. The operator
$U_j=2^{-1/2}(I-\gamma_j\gamma_{j+1})$ has eigenvalues
$e^{-i\pi/4}$ on $Q_1$ and $e^{i\pi/4}$ on $Q_\psi$, whose ratio is $i$.
By [F3], the channel exchange is therefore
$(R_1e^{i\pi/4})U_j$; its common scalar has no effect on conjugation.
[given, F3, algebra]

2.1 Let $c=s=2^{-1/2}$ and $A=\gamma_j\gamma_{j+1}$, so
$U_j=cI-sA$ and $U_j^*=cI+sA$. Multiplication using
$\gamma_jA=\gamma_{j+1}$, $A\gamma_j=-\gamma_{j+1}$,
$\gamma_{j+1}A=-\gamma_j$, and $A\gamma_{j+1}=\gamma_j$ gives
$U_j\gamma_jU_j^*=\gamma_{j+1}$ and
$U_j\gamma_{j+1}U_j^*=-\gamma_j$. Every other $\gamma_k$ commutes with
$A$, so $U_j\gamma_kU_j^*=\gamma_k$. [given, step 1.2, algebra]

2.2 For $A=\gamma_j\gamma_{j+1}$ and
$B=\gamma_{j+1}\gamma_{j+2}$, the Majorana relations give
$A^2=B^2=-I$ and $AB=-BA$. Expanding with these identities gives
$$U_jU_{j+1}U_j=-(A+B)/\sqrt2=U_{j+1}U_jU_{j+1}.$$
If $|j-k|\ge2$, then the two products $\gamma_j\gamma_{j+1}$ and
$\gamma_k\gamma_{k+1}$ commute because moving their four distinct factors
past each other contributes sign $(-1)^4=1$; hence $U_jU_k=U_kU_j$.
Thus the $U_j$ satisfy the Artin braid relations. The common scalar in
step 1.2 preserves these relations, since both sides of each relation have
the same number of generators. [given, F3, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 In the Jordan–Wigner representation,
$\gamma_{2k-1}=Z_1\cdots Z_{k-1}X_k$ and
$\gamma_{2k}=Z_1\cdots Z_{k-1}Y_k$. Direct multiplication gives
$\Pi=(-1)^m Z_1\cdots Z_m$. On a fixed parity eigenspace
$\Pi=\eta I$, so $Z_m=(-1)^m\eta Z_1\cdots Z_{m-1}$. The computational basis
in this sector is indexed by the first $m-1$ bits. Set
$\bar Z_k=Z_k$ and $\bar X_k=X_kX_m$ for $1\le k<m$. Each preserves parity;
$\bar Z_k$ reads bit $k$, while $\bar X_k$ flips bit $k$ and bit $m$, so it
flips exactly logical bit $k$. Direct multiplication also gives
$i\gamma_{2k-1}\gamma_{2k}=-Z_k$ and
$\prod_{\ell=k}^{m-1}(i\gamma_{2\ell}\gamma_{2\ell+1})
=(-1)^{m-k}X_kX_m$. Hence the logical Pauli generators are even Majorana
monomials up to scalar signs.
Projective Pauli labels form $\mathbb F_2^{2m}$. The label of $\Pi$ is
$Z_1\cdots Z_m$, and a Pauli string commutes with $\Pi$ exactly when it has
an even number of $X$ or $Y$ factors. This centralizer has dimension $2m-1$.
The $2m$ Jordan–Wigner Majorana labels form a basis: if a binary sum of them
is zero, its $X_k$ coordinate first gives $a_k+b_k=0$ for the odd/even
Majorana coefficients at wire $k$; its $Z_k$ coordinate then gives $b_k=0$,
so all coefficients vanish. Thus even Majorana products give the
codimension-one label subspace commuting with $\Pi$. The labels of
$\bar Z_1,\ldots,\bar Z_{m-1},\bar X_1,\ldots,\bar X_{m-1},\Pi$ are
independent: the $X_1,\ldots,X_{m-1}$ coordinates force all $\bar X$
exponents to vanish, the $Z_m$ coordinate forces the $\Pi$ exponent to
vanish, and then the other $Z$ coordinates force all $\bar Z$ exponents to
vanish. They therefore generate the full centralizer. On a fixed-parity
eigenspace $\Pi$ is scalar, leaving precisely the projective logical Pauli
group generated by $\bar X_k,\bar Z_k$. By step 2.1 each braid sends every
Majorana to a signed Majorana; it therefore normalizes that logical Pauli
group. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Conjugation gives a homomorphism from the projective Clifford group to
the automorphism group of the phase-aware Pauli group. That Pauli group is
finite, so its automorphism group is finite. The kernel consists of
unitaries commuting with every logical Pauli; commuting with all logical
$Z_k$ makes a unitary diagonal in the computational basis, and commuting
with each logical $X_k$ forces every diagonal entry to agree. Thus the
kernel is scalar and the projective Clifford group is finite. For $m\ge2$,
$PU(2^{m-1})$ is an infinite Hausdorff metric space by [F2]: the classes of
$\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{it},1,\ldots,1)$ are distinct as $t$ varies
modulo $2\pi$. A finite subgroup is closed in a metric space, so this braid
subgroup is not dense. [F1, F2, step 2.2, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Joint SU(5)×SU(8) closure from B6 path blocks
items.statement_or_definition:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For the normalized simultaneous six-$\tau$
Fibonacci B6 representation on
$V(\tau^6\to1)\oplus V(\tau^6\to\tau)\cong\mathbb C^5\oplus\mathbb C^8$,
the closure in $U(5)\times U(8)$ contains $SU(5)\times SU(8)$.
proof_obligations:
1.1 The common Fibonacci data in [A2] give the same normalized two-dimensional
three-strand block for $C=B_1B_2^{-1}$ in both total-charge spaces. Direct
multiplication gives determinant $1$, trace $\phi^{-2}$, and eigenvalues
$e^{i\theta},e^{-i\theta}$ with $2\cos\theta=\phi^{-2}$ on that factor;
the remaining factors contribute eigenvalue $1$. [A2, algebra]

1.2 The algebraic number $\phi^{-2}$ has minimal polynomial
$x^2-3x+1$, whose other root is $\phi^2>2$. If $e^{i\theta}$ were a root of
unity, every algebraic conjugate of $e^{i\theta}+e^{-i\theta}$ would be a
sum of two roots of unity and have absolute value at most $2$. The conjugate
$\phi^2>2$ contradicts this, so $\theta/(2\pi)$ is irrational.
[given, step 1.1, algebra]

2.1 The 24 independent Lie words in the five-dimensional proof and the
deterministically selected 63 independent Lie words in the
eight-dimensional proof are each formed from the initial tangent $X$ by
conjugations by the same generators and Lie brackets. Applying those same
word operations to $(X_5,X_8)$ gives elements of $\mathfrak g$ whose first
projections span $\mathfrak{su}(5)$ and whose second projections span
$\mathfrak{su}(8)$, respectively, by [F1]. Therefore both coordinate
projections of $\mathfrak g$ are surjective. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 Each normalized generator has determinant pair $(r^3,r^5)$ by the rank
calculations in [F1]. The joint determinant image is therefore finite, so
the identity component of the closure lies in $SU(5)\times SU(8)$ and
$\mathfrak g\subseteq\mathfrak{su}(5)\oplus\mathfrak{su}(8)$. With both
projections surjective by step 2.1, $\mathfrak g$ is a subdirect Lie
subalgebra of that product. [F1, F2, step 2.1, algebra]

3.1 For $n\ge2$, the complex Lie algebra $\mathfrak{sl}_n(\mathbb C)$ is
simple. Let $I$ be a nonzero ideal. If some $X\in I$ has an off-diagonal
entry $X_{ij}\ne0$, choose a traceless diagonal matrix $D$ whose ordered
differences $\lambda_p-\lambda_q$ ($p\ne q$) are nonzero and pairwise
distinct. Such a $D$ exists because each forbidden equality is a proper
linear hyperplane in the trace-zero diagonal subspace, and finitely many
proper hyperplanes do not cover a vector space over the infinite field
$\mathbb C$. The map $\operatorname{ad}_D$ has eigenvectors $E_{pq}$ with
these eigenvalues and is zero on diagonal matrices. Lagrange interpolation
therefore supplies a polynomial in $\operatorname{ad}_D$ that sends $X$ to
$X_{ij}E_{ij}$; since $I$ is an ideal, $E_{ij}\in I$. If instead a nonzero
$X\in I$ is diagonal, it is nonscalar because it is traceless. Choose
$i\ne j$ with $X_{ii}\ne X_{jj}$; then
$[E_{ij},X]=(X_{jj}-X_{ii})E_{ij}\in I$, again giving a matrix unit.
From $E_{ij}\in I$, bracketing with $E_{ji}$ gives
$E_{ii}-E_{jj}\in I$, and bracketing that diagonal matrix with $E_{ji}$
gives $E_{ji}\in I$. For each $k\notin\{i,j\}$,
$[E_{ki},E_{ij}]=E_{kj}$ and $[E_{jk},E_{ij}]=-E_{ik}$, so these units lie
in $I$. Then $[E_{ji},E_{ik}]=E_{jk}$ for each such $k$. We now have
$E_{kj}$ and $E_{jl}$ for every $k,l\ne j$; for $k\ne l$,
$[E_{kj},E_{jl}]=E_{kl}$. Thus every off-diagonal matrix unit lies in $I$,
and their brackets give all trace-zero diagonal matrices. Hence $I$ is the
whole algebra. This also covers $n=2$, where the steps involving $k$ are
empty.
The complexification of $\mathfrak{su}(n)$ is $\mathfrak{sl}_n(\mathbb C)$:
every traceless complex matrix is uniquely a sum $A+iB$ of traceless
skew-Hermitian matrices. A nonzero real ideal of $\mathfrak{su}(n)$ would
complexify to a nonzero ideal of $\mathfrak{sl}_n(\mathbb C)$, hence to all
of it; equality of dimensions then makes the real ideal all of
$\mathfrak{su}(n)$. Therefore $\mathfrak{su}(5)$ and $\mathfrak{su}(8)$
are simple. Their dimensions $24$ and $63$ from [F3] show they are not
isomorphic. [F3, algebra]

3.2 Define the kernel ideals
$K_5=\{x\in\mathfrak{su}(5):(x,0)\in\mathfrak g\}$ and
$K_8=\{y\in\mathfrak{su}(8):(0,y)\in\mathfrak g\}$. They are ideals because
$\mathfrak g$ projects onto both factors and is closed under brackets.
Simplicity says each kernel is either zero or the whole factor. If either is
the whole factor, surjectivity of the other projection implies
$\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{su}(5)\oplus\mathfrak{su}(8)$. If both are zero,
each projection restricts to an isomorphism from $\mathfrak g$ to its
factor, yielding an isomorphism $\mathfrak{su}(5)\cong\mathfrak{su}(8)$,
contrary to their different dimensions. Thus
$\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{su}(5)\oplus\mathfrak{su}(8)$. [F2, F3, step 2.2, step 3.1, algebra]

4.1 By [F2], the identity component of the joint closure is an embedded Lie
subgroup of $SU(5)\times SU(8)$ with this full Lie algebra. It has full
dimension and is open. The product is connected by [F4], so that open
subgroup is the entire product. Therefore the joint closure contains
$SU(5)\times SU(8)$. The only choice assumption is [A1]. [A1, F2, F4, step 3.2, algebra] ∎

items.title: Fibonacci single-qubit projective density
items.statement_or_definition:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $B_1,B_2$ be the projective Fibonacci generators on the two-dimensional
three-$\tau$, total-$\tau$ fusion space from
[[ex-qc-tqc-fibonacci-qubit-matrices]]. The subgroup they generate is dense
in $PU(2)$.
proof_obligations:
1.1 Put $C=B_1B_2^{-1}$. Using $F^2=I$, $v^2=u$, and
$r+r^{-1}=-u$, direct multiplication gives
$\det C=1$ and
$\operatorname{tr}C=r+r^{-1}+(2-r-r^{-1})u^2=u^2$; the last equality uses
$u^2+u=1$, since $(2+u)u^2=1$.
Thus the eigenvalues of the unitary $C$ are $e^{i\theta}$ and $e^{-i\theta}$,
with $2\cos\theta=u^2=\phi^{-2}$. [F1, F5, algebra]

1.2 The number $\phi^{-2}$ has minimal polynomial $x^2-3x+1$, whose other
root is $\phi^2>2$. If $e^{i\theta}$ were a root of unity, then
$e^{i\theta}+e^{-i\theta}$ would have all algebraic conjugates of absolute
value at most $2$, since every such conjugate is a sum of two roots of
unity. The conjugate $\phi^2>2$ contradicts this. Hence
$\theta/(2\pi)$ is irrational. [given, step 1.1, algebra]

2.1 Since $2\theta/(2\pi)=\theta/\pi$ is irrational, [F2] shows that the
projective powers of $C$ are dense in the circle
$T=\{[\operatorname{diag}(e^{it},e^{-it})]:t\in\mathbb R\}\subset PU(2)$
after choosing an eigenbasis. This circle is contained in the closure $H$ of
the projective braid image. By [A1] and [F3], $H$ is a Lie subgroup. Let
$q:SU(2)\to PU(2)$ be the quotient map from [F4]. In an eigenbasis,
$C-C^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(2i\sin\theta,-2i\sin\theta)$, so
$dq(C-C^{-1})$ is a nonzero tangent to $T$ and belongs to
$\operatorname{Lie}(H)$.
[A1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.2, construct]

2.2 Write $X=dq(C-C^{-1})\in\operatorname{Lie}(H)$. Conjugation by
$[B_1]$ sends $T$ to a circle with tangent $\operatorname{Ad}_{[B_1]}X$.
If these circles had the same axis, the rotation in $SO(3)$ induced by
$[B_1]$ would either preserve or reverse that axis. A reversing rotation is a
half-turn, but this projective generator has angle $3\pi/5\ne\pi$. If it
preserved the oriented axis, it would commute projectively with $C$. Choose
a determinant-one lift of $[B_1]$ to $SU(2)$, using [F4]. Its conjugate of
$C$ would then be either $C$ or $-C$, because the kernel of $q$ is
$\{\pm I\}$. The second case contradicts invariance of trace and
$\operatorname{tr}C=\phi^{-2}\ne0$, so $B_1$ would commute with $C$, and
hence with $B_2$, contrary to [F1]. Therefore the two axes are nonparallel.
Under the standard identification of $\mathfrak{so}(3)$ with
$\mathbb R^3$, the Lie bracket is the cross product up to a nonzero scalar;
the bracket of two nonparallel axes is nonzero and independent of both.
Thus $\operatorname{Lie}(H)=\mathfrak{so}(3)$ by [F3].
[A1, F1, F3, F4, step 2.1, algebra]

3.1 The identity component $H^0$ has the full dimension of connected
$SO(3)$, so it is an open subgroup. A connected group has no proper open
subgroup; therefore $H^0=SO(3)$ and $H=SO(3)$. By [F4], the projective braid
image is dense in $PU(2)$. The only choice assumption is [A1], and the
conclusion is projective; no efficient braid-length bound follows. [A1, F3, F4, step 2.2, algebra] ∎

items.title: Dense projective SU(2) image has dense determinant-one lifts
items.statement_or_definition:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $q:SU(2)\to PU(2)$ be the quotient by
$\{\pm I\}$, and let $\Gamma\le PU(2)$ be dense. Then the full inverse image
$q^{-1}(\Gamma)$ is dense in $SU(2)$. Thus projective density gives
determinant-one lifts arbitrarily close to any $SU(2)$ target, while the
choice of a lift can differ by the central sign.
proof_obligations:
1.1 Let $O$ be any nonempty open subset of $SU(2)$ and choose $u\in O$.
By [F1], there is an evenly covered neighborhood $N_0$ of $q(u)$ and a
sheet $S_0$ containing $u$ such that $q|_{S_0}:S_0\to N_0$ is a
homeomorphism. Set $S=S_0\cap O$ and $N=q(S)$. Since $S$ is open in $S_0$,
$N$ is open in $N_0$; the restriction $q|_S:S\to N$ remains a
homeomorphism. [given, F1, choose]

2.1 The open set $N$ meets $\Gamma$ by [F2]; choose
$g\in N\cap\Gamma$. Its unique lift $v\in S$ lies in $O$ and satisfies
$q(v)=g$, hence $v\in q^{-1}(\Gamma)$. Thus every nonempty open $O$ meets
$q^{-1}(\Gamma)$, which is exactly density in $SU(2)$. The only stated axiom
is [A1]. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1, choose] ∎

items.title: Fibonacci B6 approximates one logical two-qubit gate in both charge blocks
items.statement_or_definition:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $U\in U(\mathbb C^4)$ and $\delta>0$.
There is one normalized six-strand Fibonacci braid word $b$ such that its
actions $B_1(b)$ and $B_\tau(b)$ on the total-charge-$1$ and total-charge-$\tau$
blocks are simultaneously within $\delta$ of
$$T_1=U\oplus(\det U)^{-1}\in SU(5),\qquad
T_\tau=U\oplus\operatorname{diag}((\det U)^{-1},1,1,1)\in SU(8).$$
For the triple-triple computational subspace in either block, the logical
block error and leakage amplitude are each at most $\delta$. The corresponding
physical categorical braid differs from the normalized word by the common
scalar phase specified by
[[lem-qc-tqc-determinant-character-phase]].
proof_obligations:
1.1 Put $\lambda=(\det U)^{-1}$. Since $|\det U|=1$,
$|\lambda|=1$. Therefore
$\det(T_1)=\det(U)\lambda=1$ and
$\det(T_\tau)=\det(U)\lambda=1$; both targets are unitary by their
orthogonal direct-sum definitions. Hence $T_1\in SU(5)$ and
$T_\tau\in SU(8)$. [given, F2, algebra]

2.1 The open product of operator-norm $\delta$-balls around $(T_1,T_\tau)$
meets the normalized braid image because its closure contains
$SU(5)\times SU(8)$ by [A1] and [F1]. Thus one word $b$ satisfies both
block bounds at once. This is simultaneous density; separate choices of
words in the two blocks are not used. [A1, F1, step 1.1, choose]

2.2 In each block, $T_a$ acts as $U$ on the four-dimensional code and as a
unitary on its orthogonal complement. Apply [F3] to $B_1(b)$ and $T_1$,
then to $B_\tau(b)$ and $T_\tau$. The logical block error and leakage
amplitude are at most $\delta$ in both blocks. [F2, F3, step 2.1, algebra]

3.1 By [F4], the physical categorical braid is the same scalar multiple of
both normalized blocks; multiplying by a unit scalar leaves leakage
unchanged and is recorded as a projective phase for uncontrolled computation.
It must be tracked under coherent control. [F2, F4, step 2.2] ∎

items.title: Six-anyon braid target extends uniformly to fusion spectators
items.statement_or_definition:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, $n\ge2$, and a total charge $c$ with
$V(\tau^n\to c)\ne0$. The code in $3n$ $\tau$ anyons factors as
$\mathcal C_n\cong(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}\otimes V(\tau^n\to c)$.
For any adjacent pair of encoded triples, any $U\in U(4)$, and any
$\delta>0$, one normalized six-strand braid induces an ambient operator
within $\delta$ of the code-preserving ideal extension of $U$ on the entire
fixed-charge space $V(\tau^{3n}\to c)$. Consequently its logical block error
and leakage amplitude are each at most $\delta$, uniformly over all
spectator fusion paths and states that already have a component outside the
code.
proof_obligations:
1.1 Each triple has fusion factor $V(\tau^3\to\tau)\cong\mathbb C^2$.
Associating the $n$ triple charges first gives the code factorization
$(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}\otimes V(\tau^n\to c)$; the second factor records
all spectator fusion paths. This is an orthogonal fusion-tree
decomposition by [F1, F3]. [given, F1, F3, construct]

1.2 Reassociate so the chosen adjacent six strands are first. Their total
charge is $a\in\{1,\tau\}$, giving the orthogonal ambient decomposition
$$V(\tau^{3n}\to c)\cong
\bigoplus_{a=1,\tau}V(\tau^6\to a)\otimes
V(a\otimes\tau^{3n-6}\to c).$$
The second factor contains every remaining fusion path and every multiplicity
of the spectator triples. By [F3], a local six-strand braid $b$ acts as
$\bigoplus_a\rho_a(b)\otimes I$ in this decomposition. [given, F3, algebra]

2.1 For each $a$, let $T_a$ be the target extension in [F1] and define the
global ideal unitary
$\mathcal W=\bigoplus_aT_a\otimes I_{V(a\otimes\tau^{3n-6}\to c)}$,
omitting zero-dimensional summands. It preserves the triple code and acts
there as $U$ on the selected adjacent pair and identity on all other logical
and spectator factors. Joint density [F1] gives one normalized braid $b$
with $\|\rho_a(b)-T_a\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta$ for both $a=1,\tau$.
[A1, F1, step 1.1, step 1.2, choose]

2.2 Tensoring an operator $A$ with a spectator identity preserves its norm:
expand a vector in an orthonormal spectator basis to get
$\|(A\otimes I)\xi\|^2=\sum_j\|A\xi_j\|^2\le\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\|\xi\|^2$,
with equality on a maximizing unit vector tensored with one basis vector.
The norm of an orthogonal direct sum is the maximum of the block norms,
because the squared norm is the sum of the squared block norms. Hence
$\|\rho(b)-\mathcal W\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta$ on the whole ambient space.
[F1, F3, step 2.1, algebra]

3.1 Apply [F2] to $\rho(b)$ and $\mathcal W$. Their compression to the code
differs from the target by at most $\delta$, and
$(I-P)\mathcal W P=0$, so the leakage amplitude is also at most $\delta$.
The norm estimate is on the whole ambient space, so it remains valid for
inputs with prior leakage. The physical categorical word has the common
phase of [[lem-qc-tqc-determinant-character-phase]], which is harmless only
after phase matching or when reported projectively. [F1, F2, step 2.2] ∎

items.title: Arbitrary-size triple-encoded braid universality
items.statement_or_definition:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For every $n\ge1$, every total charge $c$ with
$V(\tau^n\to c)\ne0$, every unitary $U$ on $n$ logical qubits, and every
$\epsilon>0$, the triple-$\tau$ code
$$(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}\otimes V(\tau^n\to c)$$
admits a finite normalized braid word $V_b$ such that
$$\inf_{|z|=1}\|P_{\rm code}V_bP_{\rm code} -zJ(U\otimes I_S)J^*\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\epsilon,\qquad \|(I-P_{\rm code})V_bP_{\rm code}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\epsilon.$$
Here $S=V(\tau^n\to c)$ is the spectator space, $J:(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}\otimes S\to V(\tau^{3n}\to c)$ is the isometric triple-code inclusion, and the logical target is lifted as $U\otimes I_S$. The bounds are uniform over spectator fusion states. No efficient braid
word-length, search-time, or finite-precision bound is asserted.
proof_obligations:
1.1 Reassociation of the fusion trees gives the code factor
$(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}\otimes V(\tau^n\to c)$, with the second factor
retaining every spectator fusion path. For $n=1$, only $c=\tau$ occurs and
the single triple supplies the one-qubit code. [given, F2, construct]

1.2 By [F3], $U$ has a finite exact decomposition into one-qubit gates and
CNOT gates. Replace each nonadjacent two-qubit gate by the exact standard
sequence of adjacent SWAP targets, the gate on neighboring wires, and the
inverse SWAP targets. These are abstract $U(4)$ targets, not assumed to be
exact leakage-free braids. The result is a finite list of $G$ one-qubit or
adjacent two-qubit targets whose product is $U$. [F3, algebra]

2.1 If $G=0$, then $U=I$ and the empty braid proves the statement. Otherwise
put $\delta_j=\epsilon/G$ for $1\le j\le G$. For each one-qubit target
$U_j$, projective density [F1] supplies a braid whose two-dimensional
matrix is within $\delta_j$ of a phase multiple $z_jU_j$. Extend its ideal
action on the local total-$\tau$ sector by $z_jU_j$ tensored with spectator
identity, and on the local total-$1$ sector by the actual compiled braid
action. This braid-dependent extension is unitary, preserves the code, and
differs from the physical braid by at most $\delta_j$ on the full ambient
space; the complementary sector agrees exactly, so density on that sector
is not assumed. [A1, F1, F2, algebra]

2.2 For each adjacent two-qubit target, [F2] supplies a six-strand braid
and a code-preserving ideal extension with full-space error at most
$\delta_j$, including all spectator fusion sectors. The ideal one- and
two-qubit extensions therefore give a finite code-preserving target
sequence whose action on the code is $(\prod_j z_j)U$. [A1, F2, step 2.1, algebra]

3.1 Apply [F4] to the $G$ physical/ideal pairs. Their product differs in
operator norm by at most
$\sum_j\delta_j=\epsilon$. Compression to the code gives the logical block
bound, while projection to its orthogonal complement gives leakage at most
$\epsilon$. The product scalar $\prod_jz_j$, together with the common braid
phases in [F5], is the single phase removed by the projective infimum; it is
not free under coherent control. The proof gives existence only, because
[F1] and [F2] supply no useful joint B6 word-length bound. [F1, F2, F4, F5, step 2.2, algebra] ∎

items.title: Ising Clifford versus Fibonacci dense qubit
items.statement_or_definition:
In a Majorana–Ising realization satisfying
[[def-qc-tqc-ising-majorana-interface]], braid-only gates on a fixed parity
sector normalize the logical Pauli group and form a finite projective
Clifford subgroup. In the
three-$\tau$, total-$\tau$ Fibonacci sector, the two braid generators instead
generate a subgroup dense in $PU(2)$. The models therefore have different
projective gate power even though both use unitary braid matrices.
proof_obligations:
1.1 Under the stated interface [F3], the Ising conclusion is [F1]: signed
permutations of the Majorana generators normalize the finite logical Pauli
group, so the projective image is finite. [F1, F3]

1.2 The Fibonacci conclusion is [F2]: the two noncommuting generators
produce two nonparallel circle subgroups whose Lie bracket spans
$\mathfrak{so}(3)$, so their closure is $PU(2)$. A finite projective group
cannot equal this dense infinite group. [F1, F2, algebra] ∎

items.title: B6 exact rank certificates and encoded leakage budget
items.statement_or_definition:
The exact B6 certificates have determinants $17$ and $22$ modulo $31$ for
the selected $24\times24$ and $63\times63$ Lie-word minors. In the
total-charge-$1$ six-anyon space there are two natural four-dimensional code
choices: a pair-charge code and the triple code of
[[def-qc-tqc-six-anyon-encoded-subspace]]. The density argument applies to
either chosen subspace; the two definitions use different fusion trees, and
no equality of their projectors is asserted. For a circuit with $G>0$ ideal
one-qubit or adjacent two-qubit gates, assigning $\delta_j=\epsilon/G$
gives total logical block error and leakage at most $\epsilon$.
proof_obligations:
1.1 In the pairwise tree
$T_p=(((\tau_1\otimes\tau_2)\otimes(\tau_3\otimes\tau_4))
\otimes(\tau_5\otimes\tau_6))$, let $q_i\in\{0,1\}$ label the charge
$1$ or $\tau$ of pair $(2i-1,2i)$, respectively. Fusion to total charge $1$
allows exactly the strings
$$000,\quad011,\quad101,\quad110,\quad111.$$
For $000$, the intermediate charge after the first two pair outputs is $0$.
For $011,101,110,111$, it is uniquely $1,1,0,1$, respectively; each then
fuses with the last pair output to total charge $1$. A string with exactly
one $1$ has total charge $\tau$ and is inadmissible. Thus the four even
strings span a four-dimensional pair-charge code $\mathcal D_1$, and the
all-$\tau$ string $111$ spans its one-dimensional complement. Fix a unitary
associator composite from $T_p$ to the left-associated B6 tree. The triple
code $\mathcal C_1$ in [F6] is transported to that same tree by its own
fixed associator composite. Both are four-dimensional subspaces of the
five-dimensional total-charge-$1$ fusion space. The argument below treats
them as independent code choices and makes no projector-equality claim.
[A2, F6, F7, construct, algebra]

1.2 Let $\mathcal K$ be any four-dimensional subspace of the
five-dimensional total-charge-$1$ fusion space, including either
$\mathcal D_1$ or $\mathcal C_1$, and let $U\in U(\mathcal K)$. Its
orthogonal complement is one-dimensional. Define $T=U\oplus(\det U)^{-1}$
on $\mathcal K\oplus\mathcal K^\perp$; this is unitary with determinant
one, so $T\in SU(5)$. By [F1], every operator-norm neighborhood of $T$
contains a normalized B6 word. Applying [F8] to a word within $\delta$ of
$T$ gives logical block error and leakage at most $\delta$ for the selected
code. Therefore the pair-charge and triple codes each admit the same
density guarantee without identifying their subspaces. [F1, F6, F8, choose]

2.1 The five-dimensional certificate runs
research/scaffold-audit-2026-10-16/topological-quantum-computing/b6-lie-rank-certificate.py
and returns the exact minor determinant $17$ in $\mathbb F_{31}$. The
eight-dimensional deterministic selection runs
research/scaffold-audit-2026-10-16/topological-quantum-computing/b6-su8-lie-rank-certificate.py
and returns determinant $22$. Both scripts use integer arithmetic only;
[F4] proves that these nonzero reductions imply nonzero exact complex
determinants. [F1, F2, F4, algebra]

3.1 Let $G>0$ be the number of ideal gates and choose
$\delta_j=\epsilon/G$ for $1\le j\le G$. Then
$\sum_j\delta_j=\epsilon$. By [F2], each adjacent two-qubit target has a
joint braid approximation with tolerance $\delta_j$; the one-qubit targets
use the dense three-anyon representation [F5]. [F2, F5, A1, choose]

3.2 Applying [F3] to the physical and ideal gate products gives total
logical block error and leakage at most $\sum_j\delta_j=\epsilon$. For a
concrete distinction between these measurements, take $V=\mathbb C^2$,
code $\mathbb C e_0$, target $U=1$, and
$$W_\theta=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\
\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{pmatrix},\qquad0<\theta<\pi/2.$$
The compressed block is $\cos\theta$, so its logical error is
$1-\cos\theta$, while the leakage amplitude is $\sin\theta$. It has the
correct one-dimensional logical direction with reduced amplitude, not an
exactly correct block. Conversely, exact block equality forces zero leakage
by [F3]. [F3, A1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎
